stories.topicLabel: Mamdani proposes city-run grocery stores in New York
stories.analysis: The 3.0-point spread across these headlines reflects meaningfully different editorial choices. The Guardian, the most left-leaning outlet here, frames the story as a genuine policy question with its phrase "deliver cheap food for New Yorkers," centering potential benefit to residents without overt skepticism. Moving rightward, National Review dismisses the proposal outright with "Won't Last Long Enough," signaling predicted failure before any argument is made, while also invoking sympathy for small businesses through its reference to "Bodegas." Most notably, the Daily Caller sidesteps the grocery policy entirely, instead running a personal embarrassment narrative about Mamdani being "Snubbed In Awkward Scene" at a funeral — a framing that shifts focus from his policy platform to his political standing. This progression illustrates a pattern from cautious engagement with the proposal, to skeptical dismissal of its viability, to wholesale redirection away from its substance.
